draft.title: The activity series of metals
card: The activity series ranks metals by how easily they lose electrons to form positive ions. The metal at the top loses electrons most easily, so it is the most reactive.
A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from a solution of its ions. The more reactive metal goes into solution as ions and the less reactive metal forms as a solid.
Example: zinc placed in copper(II) sulfate solution becomes coated in copper, because zinc is more reactive than copper. Copper placed in zinc sulfate solution shows no change.
Common metals in order from most to least reactive include potassium, sodium, calcium, magnesium, aluminium, zinc, iron, lead, copper, silver and gold.
draft.remember: The more easily a metal loses electrons, the higher it sits, and it displaces metals below it.

a.q: Which metal ranks higher in the activity series than the others listed?
opts: The one that loses electrons most easily
The one with the highest density
The one that is hardest to cut
The one that is most often found as a solid
a.why: The series ranks metals by how easily they lose electrons, so the highest metal loses them most easily. Density and hardness are physical properties and do not set the order.
a.clue: Think about what the series ranks metals by.

b.q: Mia puts a strip of magnesium into iron(II) sulfate solution and a strip of copper into a separate beaker of iron(II) sulfate solution. What does she see?
opts: Iron forms on the magnesium only
Iron forms on the copper only
Iron forms on both strips
Iron forms on neither strip
b.why: Magnesium is more reactive than iron, so it displaces iron from solution and iron forms as a solid. Copper is less reactive than iron, so it cannot displace iron and nothing happens.
b.clue: Only a metal above iron in the series can displace iron.

a.best: The one that loses electrons most easily

b.best: Iron forms on the magnesium only
